name: How to Compare Driveway Contractor Bids

mainEntity.name: How do I compare two driveway contractor bids that use different materials?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare two driveway contractor bids that use different materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two driveway bids can look very different because they may not include the same work. One contractor may quote only the surface, while another includes demolition, excavation, base rebuilding, reinforcement, drainage correction, permits, and cleanup. The homeowner should compare line items side by side to see what is actually being purchased. Material choice matters too: concrete, asphalt, and pavers have different install methods, maintenance needs, and lifecycle costs. A higher upfront price may be worth it if it includes thicker sections, better drainage, or a stronger base. In Los Angeles County, access constraints and local approvals can also affect cost. The best comparison method is to normalize bids by asking each contractor to quote the same scope in writing, then review exclusions carefully. If a bid is much lower than the others, it often means some important work is missing rather than a true bargain. The contractor should be willing to explain those differences in plain language.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by scope, not just total price. Check the base preparation, thickness, reinforcement, drainage work, demolition, haul-away, permits, finish, and warranty for each material. A lower bid may leave out important work, while a higher bid may include better base prep or longer-lasting materials.
